title: An Updated Prospective Quantitative Analysis of Symptoms and Safety for Human Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is a noninvasive neuromodulation technique with a favorable safety profile in healthy volunteers. Participant-experienced symptoms, however, remain inconsistently measured, and prospective benchmarks are lacking. Here, we prospectively characterized symptoms associated with LIFU neuromodulation across eight studies using a standardized Report of Symptoms (ROS). We compiled 629 sessions (472 LIFU and 157 sham) in 106 healthy adults (28.1 ± 9.8 years) across eight cortical and subcortical targets (500 kHz; extracranial spatial-peak pulse-average intensity 3.9-33.3 W/cm2; mechanical index 0.5-1.4). The ROS rated 17 symptom domains from 0 (absent) to 3 (severe) before and after each session. New-onset incidence, symptom severity, and total symptom burden were compared between LIFU and sham. The same instrument was applied in 35 patients with chronic pain. Symptom profiles after LIFU were indistinguishable from sham across all 17 domains. The total symptom burden averaged approximately one domain per session and did not increase after LIFU (0.94-1.03; p = 0.120). The postintervention burden was predicted by the baseline burden (β = 0.344, p < 0.001) but not by the stimulation condition (p = 0.226). New-onset symptoms did not increase across up to 27 LIFU sessions (odds ratio = 0.99, p = 0.73) and were weakly and nonsignificantly related to acoustic intensity (ρ = 0.37). Across a prospective, sham-controlled data set, LIFU added no measurable symptom burden and was well tolerated in healthy adults, with comparable tolerability in patients. These findings establish a benchmark for the safety of human LIFU neuromodulation and a foundation for its therapeutic translation.

title: Longitudinal Impacts of Family Conflict and School Cohesion on Youth Mental Health: An ABCD Study.
journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
abstract: Adolescence is a critical period for the development of psychopathology. The current study explored associations between family and school environments and youth mental health at different stages of adolescence and potential moderating effects of biological sex. Bioecological theory posits that environmental factors at various levels, including family and school, can impact youth development and mental health outcomes. The study used data collected through follow-up year 4 from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, with a baseline sample of 11,868 youth. We examined family conflict, school environment, and youth and caregiver reports of youth internalizing and externalizing symptoms in a four-wave random intercept cross-lagged panel model. Youth externalizing and internalizing symptoms exhibited prospective associations with family conflict and school environment, particularly from ages 10-12 years. There was also evidence for the impact of school environment on internalizing symptoms between the ages of 10-13 years. Female internalizing symptoms uniquely predicted both family conflict and school environment during mid-adolescence. Results support bidirectional associations between family and school environments and youth mental health during varying developmental periods. Early detection of internalizing and externalizing symptoms is important for interrupting mutually reinforcing cycles of symptom escalation and environmental strain.

title: Multi-Omics Reveals STAT1 as a Central Regulator of Oxidative Stress-Induced Senescence in the Aging Retina.
abstract: Aging is the dominant risk factor for retinal neurodegeneration, yet the upstream regulators that coordinate senescence-associated programs across retinal cell types remain incompletely defined. Here we combined bulk RNA-seq and quantitative proteomics of retinas from naturally aged (24-month) and young (4-month) mice to define age-associated molecular programs and infer upstream regulators. We identified coordinated but imperfect transcript-protein coupling, with prominent immune and metabolic activation and concomitant repression of visual and structural pathways. Network-based integration nominated Stat1 as a convergent hub linking oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and cell fate regulation. Functionally, STAT1 induction accompanied oxidative stress-driven senescence in human ARPE-19 cells; ectopic STAT1 expression was sufficient to elicit senescence-like transcriptional changes, increase reactive oxygen species, and activate inflammasome-associated signaling, whereas STAT1 knockdown attenuated TBHP-induced senescence, reduced p53 and ASC upregulation, and blocked stress-induced nuclear accumulation of STAT1. Re-analysis of aging retina single-cell RNA-seq data further localized Stat1 expression primarily to horizontal cells and glial populations, while Stat1 target programs were engaged across multiple retinal cell types, consistent with compartmentalized initiation and multicellular propagation of inflammatory aging cues. Together, these data establish STAT1 as a mechanistic driver and cell-context-dependent marker of retinal aging, providing a rationale for targeting STAT1-centered pathways to delay or mitigate age-related retinal degeneration.

title: Seizure quantification using wearable devices.
abstract: Accurate assessment of seizure occurrence is central to treatment optimization, risk stratification, and management of epilepsy, yet remains largely dependent on patient-reported seizure diaries, which are frequently incomplete and unreliable. Wearable technologies have emerged as promising tools to enable objective and continuous seizure monitoring by capturing seizure-induced physiological signals. Over the past decade, substantial progress has been made in the development and clinical validation of wearable seizure detection systems, particularly for generalized convulsive seizures, where high sensitivity can be achieved, whereas detection of nonconvulsive seizures remains more limited. However, translating detection into clinically meaningful seizure quantification presents important challenges, including variability in performance across seizure types, patient populations, and individual physiological responses, as well as differences between controlled and real-world settings. This narrative review critically examines wearable technologies for seizure quantification, integrating recent clinical evidence and expert perspectives. We discuss key sensor modalities, including accelerometry, electrocardiography-derived features such as heart rate variability, multimodal biosignal integration, and emerging ultra-long-term wearable and subcutaneous electroencephalographic systems. Each modality offers specific advantages and limitations depending on seizure type and clinical context. Attention is also given to the importance of user trust, adherence, and data quality as key determinants of clinical utility. We further examine the role of wearable seizure quantification in clinical practice, including treatment monitoring, tele-epileptology, and clinical trials, as well as potential future contributions to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy risk assessment. With continued technological advances and robust real-world clinical validation, wearable systems have the potential to transform seizure monitoring and support more precise, data-driven epilepsy care.

title: Intrasubject Reconfiguration of the Cortical Gradients' Topological Properties With Cognitive States.
abstract: Cortical gradients have been shown to be an effective technique to study the functional organization of the brain by capturing patterns of functional similarities. Until now, most studies have focused on analyzing cortical gradients derived from resting-state fMRI. With recent work highlighting the changes that functional brain networks undergo during various cognitive loads, there is a need to investigate whether cortical gradients are also sensitive to different cognitive demands, and to what degree. In this context, we collected a sample of 138 healthy individuals aged 12-25, each of whom completed a resting-state fMRI scan as well as three task fMRI scans (social prospection, spatial working memory, and verbal working memory). All data were analyzed to examine the task dependence of cortical gradients' topological properties. By employing the measures of network gradient dispersions as well as networks centroid distances, we revealed that alterations specific to each task occurred in topological properties of gradients involving both transmodal and unimodal networks, such as the executive control network varying between each task condition and the resting-state condition. This work highlights the promise of applying cortical gradients to task-based fMRI data, revealing the condition-sensitive nature of certain cortical gradients' topological properties.

title: Two-stage spatiotemporal graph neural network framework for seizure onset zone localization.
abstract: Accurate localization of the seizure onset zone (SOZ) is critical for the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy. Intracranial electroencephalography captures high-resolution seizure dynamics, but interpreting complex spatiotemporal patterns across implanted electrodes is clinically challenging. We propose a two-stage, uncertainty-aware framework for SOZ localization that integrates patient-specific seizure modeling with cross-patient probabilistic ranking to estimate the likelihood of each electrode belonging to the SOZ. The framework was evaluated on a bi-institutional cohort of 36 patients (20 with good surgical outcome, 16 with poor surgical outcome), comprising 184 seizures. In the first stage, a patient-specific spatiotemporal graph neural network modeled seizure onset as a network-level transition using directed functional connectivity graphs derived from burst-integrated electrophysiological features. Trained solely to detect preictal-to-ictal transitions, this model generated electrode probability trajectories without SOZ supervision. In the second stage, these trajectories were summarized into interpretable descriptors and used to train a patient-agnostic classifier assigning SOZ likelihood scores to electrodes. Evaluation and hyperparameter optimization were performed using nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation restricted to good outcome patients, ensuring strict patient-level separation between training, validation, and test data. Seizure onset detection was stable across patients, with comparable binary cross-entropy values between outcome groups (median = .495 vs. .438, p = .108). In good outcome patients, SOZ electrodes were prioritized among top-ranked contacts (area under the curve = .86 ± .06), with all patients exhibiting at least one SOZ electrode within the top positions. In poor outcome patients, predictions exhibited reduced spatial separability, lower likelihood magnitudes, and near-zero confidence gaps, reflecting attenuated model confidence. This two-stage framework integrates spatial interactions, temporal dynamics, and probabilistic ranking within a pipeline. By providing graded SOZ likelihood estimates and uncertainty-aware prioritization, the approach is a decision-support tool to assist hypothesis refinement during presurgical evaluation rather than as a standalone diagnostic system.

title: Association of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with 6-month cognitive outcomes and white matter lesion progression in patients with cerebral small vessel disease and cognitive impairment.
abstract: To examine the association of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) with 6-month cognitive outcomes and white matter lesion progression in patients with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and cognitive impairment. A retrospective cohort study design was used. Data from 427 patients with CSVD and cognitive impairment who attended the Department of Neurology of our hospital from January 2022 to December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Based on treatment documented in the medical records, patients were classified into an rTMS group (n = 228), who had received 10 Hz high-frequency rTMS over the left DLPFC as part of routine clinical care, and a control group (n = 199), who had received conventional pharmacotherapy alone. Both groups received standardized basic CSVD treatment; the rTMS group additionally received rTMS once daily, 5 days per week, for 2 consecutive weeks (10 sessions). Complete baseline and 6-month neuropsychological and MRI records were required for inclusion; therefore, all 427 patients had complete data for the prespecified outcomes and no imputation was required. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change from baseline in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score at 6 months (ΔMoCA). Secondary outcomes included changes in MMSE, TMT-A, TMT-B, Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure delayed recall, MoCA responder rates, imaging outcomes, safety, and exploratory subgroup analyses. A propensity score matching (PSM) sensitivity analysis was performed for ΔMoCA, MoCA responder rates, and WMHV change. The rTMS group showed significantly greater delta-MoCA than the control group (mean difference [MD] = 1.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.56-1.66, p .05). A PSM sensitivity analysis (195 matched pairs) yielded consistent results for the primary outcome (MD = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.64-1.81, p < .001, d = 0.29). In exploratory subgroup analyses (not prespecified), cognitive severity (interaction p < .001) and diabetes status (interaction p = .014) suggested potential treatment effect modification, with numerically greater benefit in patients with moderate cognitive impairment and those without diabetes. The overall incidence of adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (15.4% vs. 13.6%, p = .602); all events were mild to moderate and transient, and no serious adverse events occurred. In this retrospective cohort study, high-frequency rTMS over the left DLPFC was associated with greater improvement in long-term cognitive function in patients with CSVD and cognitive impairment, particularly in global cognition, executive function, and memory, with a favorable safety profile. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that cognitive severity and diabetes status may influence treatment outcomes, warranting prospective validation. rTMS did not significantly delay white matter lesion progression; its cognitive benefits may be mediated primarily through enhanced neuroplasticity and functional network reorganization rather than structural lesion modification.

title: β-glucan mitigates necrotizing enterocolitis-induced long-term cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and restoring tryptophan metabolite IAA-mediated gut-brain signaling.
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal disorder prevalent in preterm infants, and most NEC survivors suffer from persistent cognitive deficits and neurodevelopmental disorders, with no targeted therapeutic approaches available to date. β-glucan has been documented to regulate gut microbiota, suppress inflammation, and exert neuroprotective effects, yet its efficacy and molecular mechanisms against NEC-associated cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. In this study, we established a mouse NEC model with β-glucan intervention to explore its gut-brain axis protective effects. Behavioral assessments verified that β-glucan significantly rescued NEC-induced cognitive impairments, with comparable therapeutic effects between low and high doses. Multi-omics analyses demonstrated that β-glucan effectively reversed NEC-triggered gut microbiota dysbiosis and restored disrupted tryptophan metabolism, notably elevating the level of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). Fecal microbiota transplantation and exogenous IAA supplementation recapitulated the neuroprotective phenotypes of β-glucan, which inhibited excessive hippocampal microglial activation and neuroinflammation, and repaired impaired synaptic ultrastructure and plasticity. Further mechanistic validation confirmed that IAA mediated neuroprotection via activating the AHR/MAP2K3/p38 signaling cascade. Collectively, β-glucan alleviates NEC-related cognitive injury through modulating the gut microbiota-tryptophan metabolism-IAA axis and subsequent AHR/MAP2K3/p38 signaling activation. This study elucidates a novel gut‒brain axis regulatory mechanism of β-glucan, providing reliable preclinical evidence for the clinical prevention and treatment of long-term neurodevelopmental complications in NEC survivors.

title: Spatial correspondence between spontaneous brain activity alterations and normative molecular and neurochemical architecture in pediatric epilepsy.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
abstract: Pediatric epilepsy is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed brain networks, but the molecular context of spontaneous brain activity alterations remains incompletely understood. This study investigated regional spontaneous brain activity alterations in pediatric epilepsy and their spatial correspondence with normative molecular reference maps. In this observational case-control neuroimaging study, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data from 44 children with epilepsy and 44 healthy controls selected using group-level frequency matching for age and sex were analyzed. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional ALFF (fALFF) were compared between groups. The unthresholded signed ALFF case-control t-map was subsequently parcellated using the Schaefer 2018 400-parcel atlas. The 200 left-hemisphere cortical parcels were spatially related to normative adult Allen Human Brain Atlas gene-expression data using partial least squares (PLS) regression, and the whole-cortex ALFF map was compared with 39 normative adult neurotransmitter maps. First partial least squares component (PLS1) explained 36.42% of the variance in the left-hemisphere cortical ALFF map and was significant under 10,000 spherical spin permutations (P_spin=0.0004); regional PLS1 scores were positively associated with ALFF t-values (ρ=0.5650, P_spin=0.0004). PLS1-associated genes were enriched for synaptic, ion-transport, membrane-regulation, and neuronal-projection annotations, and inhibitory-neuron gene sets showed significant enrichment (P=0.0014). The signed ALFF map showed inverse spatial associations with the MU_CARFENTANIL_c11 μ-opioid receptor map (median Spearman ρ=-0.3317, mean Fisher z=-0.3448, P_spin=0.0003, q_FDR =0.0044) and the mGluR5_abp_hc73_smart map (median Spearman ρ=-0.2610, mean Fisher z=-0.2672, P_spin=0.0001, q_FDR =0.0022). These findings provide indirect atlas-based spatial molecular context for the pediatric imaging phenotype. Because the molecular maps were derived from independent adult reference datasets, the associations should not be interpreted as patient-specific gene-expression or receptor measurements, causal mechanisms, or developmentally matched molecular abnormalities.

title: Clinical Heterogeneity in Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1: Identifying Phenotype Categories Using Unsupervised Clustering.
authors: de Kok J W T M
abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a genetic multisystem disorder with a wide variability in symptom severity and symptom co-occurrence. This study aimed to identify homogeneous patient subgroups in DM1 with distinct disease characteristics, determine key features underlying these subgroups, and evaluate their potential to inform clinical care and individualized therapy. Adult patients with genetically confirmed DM1 were assessed during annual visits to the Dutch DM1 expert center using standardized examinations and questionnaires to characterize disease burden. K-means cluster analysis was conducted on 10 baseline parameters that reflect the multisystemic disease impact of DM1. External validation was conducted using baseline data from the END-DM1 natural history study. Six hundred fifty-eight Dutch patients with DM1 were included, with a mean age of 45.33 ± 14.30 years and a mean disease duration of 13.24 ± 10.42 years. Four clusters were identified, including 166, 169, 149, and 174 patients. Cluster 1 included patients with severe myotonia, gastrointestinal complaints, fatigue and daytime sleepiness, and reduced ability to perform daily activities. Cluster 2 included patients severely affected across all domains except for myotonia. Cluster 3 showed reduced respiratory functioning and reduced ability to perform daily activities. Cluster 4 included patients with minimal symptoms. Clustering of 581 patients in the external data set resulted in similar cluster profiles. Four distinct clinical subgroups with characteristic multisystemic profiles were identified and independently validated. These findings demonstrate that DM1 heterogeneity reflects qualitatively different disease patterns rather than a simple severity continuum and provide foundation for more targeted patient stratification in clinical trials and health care.

title: Survival determinants and treatment patterns in a European multi-center cohort of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a distinct head and neck malignancy characterized by marked geographic and ethnic variability, with most studies originating from endemic Asian regions. However, the disease also occurs in non-endemic populations, where prognostic factors and treatment outcomes may differ. This study aimed to evaluate overall survival (OS) in a European multi-institutional cohort of patients with NPC and to assess the impact of disease stage and chemotherapy exposure on survival outcomes. A retrospective multicenter study was conducted including patients diagnosed with NPC in six oncology centers across Romania, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Eligible patients had histologically confirmed NPC and a minimum follow-up of five years. Clinical, demographic, staging, and treatment data were collected from medical records. OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. Univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to identify prognostic factors. A total of 416 patients were included, with a mean age of 48.2 years and a predominance of males (68%). Most patients presented with advanced-stage disease (83.7%). Concurrent chemotherapy was administered in 73.3% of cases. Median survival was 204 months in patients receiving chemotherapy and 187 months in those without chemotherapy, with no significant difference between groups (p = 0.85). Chemotherapy exposure was not independently associated with OS in multivariable analysis. Increasing age was identified as an independent prognostic factor associated with higher mortality risk (HR 1.03 per year, p < 0.001). In this European multicenter cohort, OS in NPC patients was primarily influenced by age, as demonstrated by independent multivariable Cox regression (HR 1.03 per year, p < 0.001), while concurrent chemotherapy was not independently associated with improved survival. Disease stage was used as a stratification variable in the multivariable model to account for non-proportional hazards; accordingly, no hazard ratio for stage is estimated. Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested higher survival probabilities in early-stage disease, though this difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank p = 0.099). Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the role of systemic therapy in non-endemic populations.

title: EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.
abstract: Functional enrichment of transcriptomic datasets can be constrained by incomplete annotation, uneven identifier recognition, and uncertainty about which organism annotation resource provides the most informative functional context. EchoGO is a reproducible downstream framework that retains target GOseq enrichment as the primary functional evidence while evaluating the same transcriptomic response across researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. Evidence is assembled at the GO-term level with its analytical and organism provenance, allowing researchers to distinguish functions supported by the target analysis, functions also recovered through alternative annotation contexts, and additional context-derived hypotheses. Semantic reduction, gene-sharing networks, visualisation, and reporting organise this evidence into interpretable biological summaries. Validation across a reference-rich zebrafish dataset and two annotation-limited Gammarus pulex comparisons revealed contrasting patterns of annotation-context dependence. In zebrafish, 42 of 44 target GO terms were also recovered through alternative fish contexts, while additional contexts expanded the range of functional hypotheses. In G. pulex, limited identifier representation restricted contextual analysis; recovered functions were predominantly translation-related in one comparison and also included contractile biology in the other. EchoGO provides a traceable framework for examining how annotation availability and organism context shape functional interpretation while preserving the target analysis as the experimental anchor.

title: Axonal transcriptome remodeling during PGE2 induced sensitization identifies Tnfrsf12a/FN14 as a regulator of sensory neuron excitability.
abstract: Axonal mRNA translation is a key regulator of neuronal plasticity, yet its contribution to inflammatory pain remains poorly defined. Here, we combine compartmentalized dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron cultures with RNA sequencing to map axonal and somatic transcriptomes and their remodeling following prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)-induced sensitization. We identify a conserved axonal transcriptome across embryonic and adult neurons, enriched for ribosomal and mitochondrial functions, supporting sustained local translation and metabolic activity. PGE2 triggers compartment-specific transcriptomic reprogramming, with axons showing enrichment of inflammatory and pain-related pathways, while somatic responses favor translational processes. Functionally, axonal PGE2 exposure enhances neuronal excitability and drives retrograde sensitization. Integrative analyses identify Tnfrsf12a (Fn14) as an axonally localized, PGE2-responsive transcript whose local knockdown reduces excitability and attenuates sensitization. These findings establish axonal transcriptome dynamics as key drivers of peripheral sensitization and highlight axonally localized mRNAs as spatially precise therapeutic targets for inflammatory pain.

title: Remodeling of synaptome architecture following traumatic brain injury.
abstract: In the brain, excitatory synapse diversity is organized into a brainwide synaptome architecture. Traumatic brain injury is associated with synapse loss, but its impact upon synaptome architecture is unknown. Using synaptome mapping across 222 brain regions in mice, we show that lateral fluid percussion injury induces a progressive and distributed reorganization of excitatory synapse populations over 28 days. Although whole-brain synapse number is preserved, specific molecular types and subtypes of synapses exhibit region- and time-dependent vulnerability. At 7 days after injury, synapse types with rapid turnover of the postsynaptic scaffold protein PSD95 are preferentially reduced. However, by 28 days, they have increased, whereas those synapses with slow turnover are reduced. Microglial activation correlated with this synaptome remodeling in a temporally structured manner. These findings reveal a two-phase, proteostasis-linked reprogramming of synaptome architecture, suggesting that large-scale rebalancing of molecularly distinct synapse populations is a general mechanism underlying injury-induced brain plasticity.

title: Outdoor Air Pollution Exposure Alters Fear Regulation and Fear-Related Neural Circuitry in Adolescence.
abstract: Air pollution is an emerging risk factor for anxiety in youth, but the neurobehavioral mechanisms remain unclear. Anxiety disorders are associated with altered fear-related learning, processes refined across adolescence. We examined whether adolescents with high versus low past-month exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) differ in fear-related learning. Adolescents (N = 102; 55% female; ages 10-17 years) completed a Pavlovian fear conditioning, extinction, and recall paradigm. PM2.5 exposure was estimated using a spatiotemporal model and categorized as low versus high via the Environmental Protection Agency's annual standard (9 μg/m3). Fear responses were assessed using skin conductance responses (SCRs), behavioral avoidance, and self-reported fear. Linear mixed-effects models tested associations between PM2.5 group, task phase, and conditioned stimulus type, adjusting for age, sex, and neighborhood disadvantage. In a subset (n = 68), neuroimaging analyses examined activation within fear-related regions of interest. Compared with the low group, the high group exhibited greater SCRs and subjective fear in response to conditioned threat cues during conditioning. The high-exposure group demonstrated a greater return of fear during recall, reflected in elevated SCRs in response to the extinguished cue and sustained subjective fear. Across phases, the high-exposure group exhibited higher SCRs overall. Neuroimaging analyses showed greater right amygdala activation during conditioning and extinction and greater left insula activation during recall in youths with high versus low exposure. Compared with low PM2.5 exposure, high PM2.5 exposure was associated with altered fear processing across subjective, physiological, and neural levels, suggesting fear dysregulation as a potential mechanistic link between air pollution and anxiety.

title: Diversity, equity and inclusion considerations in the design of digital mental health interventions for psychosis: A scoping review.
abstract: Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) are increasingly used to support people with psychosis. However, little is known about how diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) are considered in their design. In this review, DEI was operationalised as design considerations relating to access, content, appearance, and stakeholder involvement, employed to support development of equitable and inclusive DMHI, and evaluated using an adapted Culturally Informed Design Framework. While stakeholder engagement is frequently reported, the extent to which design processes systematically address DEI domains remains unclear. This scoping review examines what design approaches have been used, the nature of stakeholder involvement, and the DEI domains considered in DMHI development for psychosis. A systematic search across six databases identified 167 eligible studies, describing 55 DMHIs. Data were extracted and synthesised. Thirteen interventions (23.6%) explicitly named a design approach, with user-, person-, or human-centred design most frequently reported. Thirty-one interventions (56.4%) reported some level of stakeholder engagement in design, most commonly involving people with lived experience of psychosis and clinicians. Forty-three interventions (78.2%) were reported as addressing at least one DEI-related feature. At the subdomain level, literacy (n = 15), system requirements (n = 16), psychosis-specific adaptations (n = 14), and diverse visual representation (n = 13) were among the most frequently reported considerations, whereas cultural adaptation (n = 3), availability in languages beyond English (n = 3), and environmental tailoring (n = 5) were rarely reported. Interventions characterised by sustained stakeholder engagement across multiple stages of development tended to demonstrate broader DEI coverage, although inclusion was rarely articulated as an explicit design goal. These findings highlight that while participatory design approaches are commonly employed, published reports indicated limited and uneven integration of DEI considerations in DMHI design. To support equity and inclusion, DMHI development should adopt a theoretically-informed design approach with stakeholder involvement throughout and comprehensive targeting of DEI domains.

title: Endogenous suspension of phenomenal consciousness during extended cessation: Regional homogeneity analysis of multi-participant 7T fMRI of an advanced meditative endpoint.
abstract: Extended cessation (EC) is a rare advanced meditative state characterized by the voluntary absence of reportable phenomenal experience, followed by reproducible aftereffects including immense mental clarity, equanimity, and peace. EC offers an endogenous model for investigating the mechanisms of consciousness. In a small-N case study (N = 3) using ultra-high-resolution 7T functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) with dense within-subject sampling, we quantified whole-brain activity and related it to chemoarchitecture and cognitive maps. EC is marked by increased activity in unimodal sensory cortices and viscerosensory brainstem nuclei, and down-regulation in transmodal regions, subcortex and brainstem. Meta-analytic cognitive decoding linked EC to perceptual clarity and attentional processes, and away from distress-related domains. Multivariate coupling to normative neurotransmitter maps revealed that EC-related connectivity changes covaried with histaminergic H3 receptors topology. These findings constrain prevailing theories of consciousness by demonstrating that loss of experience need not entail global neural suppression, and supports accounts emphasizing selective precision modulation and hierarchical decoupling. More broadly, EC demonstrates that consciousness can cease without global suppression, suggesting a potential "reset" mechanism that fosters equanimity and the potential for flourishing.

title: Response to methodological considerations in nutritional intervention trial among patients receiving methadone maintenance treatment.
Paclitaxel-induced disruption of lysosome motility and function in DRG neurons.
abstract: Lysosomal trafficking and homeostasis are biological functions that are pivotal for DRG neurons, given their metabolic demands and extremely long axons. Previous studies indicate that lysosomal signaling is altered in a mouse model of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) and that blocking mitogen activated protein kinase-associated kinase (MNK1/2) signaling can alleviate pain behaviors in CIPN. Here, we investigated lysosome dynamics and lysosome-associated signaling in a mouse model of CIPN induced by paclitaxel (PTX), a chemotherapeutic agent used for various types of cancer. Using spinning disk super-resolution microscope (SPINSR), we demonstrate that PTX treatment in vivo causes reduced lysosome motility observed in vitro. PTX likewise drives the accumulation of Sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1), also known as P62, in cultured mouse DRG neurons, indicating lysosomal dysfunction in DRG neurons. The transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, was also upregulated in the nucleus of cultured mouse DRG neurons treated with PTX. In line with this, increased lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) expression was observed in PTX-treated mice. Given that our previous work demonstrated PTX treatment increases MNK1/2-eIF4E signaling in DRG neurons, we examined whether MNK1/2 inhibition could rescue lysosomal dysfunction. Treatment with Tomivosertib (eFT508), a potent MNK1/2 inhibitor, restored P62 levels in DRG neurons of PTX-treated mice and reduced TFEB in DRG treated in vitro. To establish translation relevance, we further show that PTX elevates phosphorylated eiF4E (p-eIF4E) in human DRG neurons, and concurrent eFT508 administration attenuates this effect. Collectively, these findings indicated that PTX disrupts lysosome trafficking and biogenesis, and that MNK inhibition with eFT508 restores lysosomal signaling and can serve as a neuroprotective strategy for CIPN.

title: IRF8 deficiency causes anxiety-like behavior with sex differences.
abstract: Anxiety disorder is a serious psychiatric disease that affects women more than men and disrupts patients' daily lives. It is often comorbid with major depression and other mental diseases. Various underlying mechanisms have been proposed, such as neurotransmitters and neuroanatomical disruptions, and more recently, oxidative stress; however, much remains unclear, including the role of glial cells. Here, we investigated the role of IRF8 in anxiety-like behavior using mouse models. IRF8 is a transcription factor expressed primarily in microglia in the brain. A battery of behavioral tests revealed that female IRF8 knockout (IRF8KO) mice show increased anxiety-like behavior relative to male IRF8KO and wild-type mice. Female IRF8KO mice also exhibited a higher tendency for obsessive-compulsive-like disorder. However, these behavioral abnormalities were not observed when IRF8 was deleted postnatally, indicating that it acts during the fetal stage to control anxiety-like behavior. Transcriptome analysis revealed that IRF8 deficiency leads to redox dysregulation. Further, 2',7'-dichlorofluorescin diacetate (DCFDA) staining for microglia demonstrated that female IRF8KO microglia produce higher levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) compared to WT and male IRF8KO counterparts. Detailed RNA-seq analysis, however, did not reveal specific genes that cause high ROS production in female cells. In sum, this work demonstrates that IRF8 in microglia plays a major role in controlling anxiety and OCD-like behavior with potential sex-specific differences.

title: Revisiting the longitudinal relationships among depressive symptoms, emotion regulation, and perceived social support: evidence from a random intercept cross-lagged panel model.
journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
abstract: The bidirectional relationship between depressive symptoms and perceived social support has been widely reported, and emotion regulation is considered an important mediating mechanism between the two. However, prior studies have not rigorously distinguished stable between-person differences from within-person dynamic changes. The present study applied a Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM) to examine the bidirectional relationship between depressive symptoms and perceived social support at the within-person level, as well as the mediating roles of cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression. A total of 1,390 Chinese college students contributed data to a three-wave study with three-month intervals. RI-CLPM was used to separate between-person and within-person effects. After controlling for between-person differences, one indirect pathway was significant at the within-person level: elevated depressive symptoms at T1 predicted decreased cognitive reappraisal at T2, which in turn predicted reduced perceived social support at T3. Cognitive reappraisal at T2 also negatively predicted depressive symptoms at T3. The direct bidirectional paths between depressive symptoms and perceived social support, as well as all indirect paths through expressive suppression, were not significant. Cognitive reappraisal may play a role in the erosion of perceived social support associated with depressive symptoms. These findings support further testing of whether reappraisal training can help preserve perceived social support among individuals with elevated depressive symptoms.

title: Digital pathways to self-harm: Modafinil-induced mania and AI-assisted operationalization of suicidal intent in a law student: a case report.
abstract: Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting (eugeroic) agent increasingly used off-label for cognitive enhancement. Although generally regarded as having a favorable psychiatric safety profile, it can precipitate manic or hypomanic episodes in vulnerable individuals, and the boundary between a self-limited substance-induced episode and the unmasking of an underlying mood disorder is not always clear at presentation. We report the case of a 20-year-old female law student admitted to the emergency unit after a suicide attempt by polypharmacy overdose during escalating off-label modafinil use. A notable feature was her use of an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational platform to inform about the preparation of the attempt: the AI did not generate her suicidal motivation but contributed to operationalizing an already-formed intent. The acute presentation was characterized by logorhoea, affective expansiveness, and behavioral disinhibition, initially consistent with a substance-induced manic episode. Over the three-month follow-up, however, subsyndromal hypomanic features persisted after discontinuation of modafinil and after withdrawal of a serotonergic antidepressant, while the patient was maintained on a mood stabilizer - raising the possibility that modafinil acted as a precipitant unmasking an underlying bipolar diathesis. This case illustrates modafinil's potential to precipitate affective destabilization in a high-achieving young person under sustained academic pressure, and the difficulty of distinguishing a transient substance-induced episode from an emerging bipolar-spectrum disorder without longitudinal follow-up. It also highlights an emerging risk: the role of large language models (LLMs) in operationalizing - rather than originating - suicidal intent. The case underscores the need for careful psychiatric screening before prescribing wakefulness-promoting agents, for continued longitudinal monitoring, and for attention to patients' interactions with AI platforms during crisis assessment.

title: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder as a Prodromal Manifestation of Alpha-Synucleinopathies.
abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia in which patients physically act out their dreams due to loss of the normal muscle paralysis that occurs during REM sleep. It is now recognized that isolated RBD (iRBD) is strongly associated with future development of α-synuclein-related neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). It is seen that most patients with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD eventually develop a clinically defined synucleinopathy, often after a long symptom-free interval. This long prodromal phase makes iRBD a unique clinical model for studying the earliest stages of neurodegeneration, before the onset of clear motor or cognitive disability. α-synuclein pathology frequently begins in the lower brainstem and autonomic nervous system, affecting REM sleep regulatory circuits early in the disease process. As pathology spreads, dopaminergic, cholinergic, and cortical systems become involved, leading to the gradual emergence of motor, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms. As a result, many individuals with iRBD exhibit subtle non-motor features such as hyposmia, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, anxiety, and mild cognitive changes years before a formal neurological diagnosis is made. Recent advances have improved the ability to identify patients at the highest risk of near-term phenoconversion. Quantitative measures of REM sleep without atonia, dopamine transporter imaging, autonomic testing, and emerging molecular biomarkers, including α-synuclein seed amplification assays, have shown promise in risk stratification. In addition, cognitive changes may occur earlier than previously recognized, particularly in patients with iRBD who also demonstrate hyposmia or dopaminergic dysfunction. Management of RBD remains largely symptomatic and focuses on injury prevention and sleep stabilization. While clonazepam and melatonin remain first-line therapies, alternative treatments including sodium oxybate, serotonergic agents, cannabinoids, and modulation of the gut-brain axis through probiotic supplementation have also been explored. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge regarding the clinical features, mechanisms, biomarkers, and management of RBD as a prodromal manifestation of α-synucleinopathies, with emphasis on its importance for early diagnosis and future disease-modifying research.

title: Species-specific sensorimotor noise levels explain saccadic suppression strength differences between macaques and zebrafish.
abstract: Active sensing requires integrating information about self-generated movements and afferent inputs. However, such information is inherently variable and relies on uncertain extrapolations. Saccadic suppression of visual sensitivity is a classic example of sensory motor integration. Here, we used a control theory model based on efficient state estimation to predict that optimal saccadic suppression strength depends on the time-dependent magnitude of unexplained sensory and motor variability. Using two drastically different species, macaques and zebrafish larvae, we experimentally measured saccadic suppression in the superior colliculus and the homologous optic tectum. Species-specific oculomotor noise was quantified experimentally, and sensory noise was estimated. We found that inter-species differences in sensory and motor noise levels, as well as their theoretically predicted impacts on visual sensitivity, are consistent with observed differences in saccadic suppression strength. Our results highlight the importance of computational resource limits of the brain for understanding performance differences that have evolved in homologous brain areas.

title: Zinc Supplementation Attenuates Pro-Inflammatory Cytokine Responses in a Cuprizone-Induced Rat Model of Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder marked by neuroinflammation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration. Zinc is crucial for immune regulation, but its impact on inflammatory cytokines in MS is not well understood. This study examined how dietary zinc status influences pro-inflammatory cytokine release in spinal cord tissue using a cuprizone-induced rat model of MS. The experimental cohort comprised 46 adult male Wistar rats, randomly allocated into five groups: Control (n=6) and four experimental groups "G" (n=10 each). G1 served as the untreated Control. G2, Sham-MS received daily oral gavage of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) solution-used as the vehicle for cuprizone-administered at 1% of their daily feed intake for 8 weeks. G3, G4, and G5 underwent MS induction via daily gavage of cuprizone dissolved in CMC at 1% of daily feed intake over the same period. G4 was maintained on a zinc-deficient diet (50 µg/kg zinc), whereas G5 received intraperitoneal zinc sulfate supplementation at 5 mg/kg/day. Disease progression was assessed by Rotarod performance and Myelin Basic Protein gene expression. Spinal cord levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 were measured by ELISA. Multiple sclerosis induction significantly increased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels (p <0.05), especially in zinc-deficient rats. Zinc supplementation attenuated these cytokine elevations, normalizing them to control levels (p <0.05). Functional and molecular data confirmed reduced disease severity with zinc repletion. Our findings reveal that zinc status is a critical modulator of neuroinflammation in an experimental MS model. Inflammatory cytokine levels in the spinal cord were significantly higher in both MS and zinc-deficient MS groups, confirming local inflammation associated with demyelination. Furthermore, zinc supplementation demonstrated a regulatory effect by suppressing the increase in inflammatory cytokines in the experimental MS model. These results may point to the therapeutic potential of zinc in MS management.

title: Using Genetics to Understand the Role of Lifestyle and Socioeconomic Factors in the Relationship Between Major Depressive Disorder and Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are global health problems that frequently co-occur. The bidirectional causal relationship between them is well established, although the potential mediators remain understudied. Here, we investigated the role of lifestyle and socioeconomic traits as mediators of the MDD-T2D relationship using genetic data. Using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, we tested whether the genetic correlation (r g ) between MDD (n = 2,000,702) and T2D (n = 1,812,017) was influenced by lifestyle (physical activity and sedentary time [n = 95,776], cigarettes per day [n = 618,489], and drinks per week [n = 941,280]) and socioeconomic (educational attainment [n = 293,723] and poverty factor [n = 453,689]) traits. Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, using both GWAS and UK Biobank data, were conducted to investigate potential causal relationships. Finally, we applied mediation analysis to quantify the indirect effect of potential mediators. The strong genetic correlation between MDD and T2D (r g = 0.184, p = 3.5 × 10-37) was attenuated when accounting for cigarettes per day (partial r g = 0.098), physical activity (partial r g = 0.141), educational attainment (partial r g = 0.115), and poverty (partial r g = 0.118). MR demonstrated that a higher genetic liability to MDD and T2D was associated with higher cigarettes per day, poverty, and lower education. MR showed that higher education was associated with lower odds of MDD and T2D, while poverty was associated with higher odds of both conditions. Mediation analysis demonstrated that genetic liability to education and poverty traits substantially mediated the causal relationship in both directions: 28.67% and 24.98% for MDD→T2D and 34.3% and 29.87% for T2D→MDD, respectively. Our findings highlight the role of socioeconomic traits in the MDD-T2D relationship and demonstrate both the strength and limitations of using MR for investigating complex traits. Further research incorporating gene-environment interactions, policy implications, and diverse populations is needed to better understand this relationship.

title: Japan's regulations on the experimental use of wild-caught Japanese macaques and its historical context.
abstract: Non-human primates (NHPs) have long been indispensable to drug discovery and biomedical research, particularly in fields such as neuroscience and immunology. At the same time, because many NHP species are threatened with extinction, the use of wild-caught NHPs in research has become increasingly restricted internationally, and laboratory NHPs are supplied primarily through captive breeding. Against this global backdrop, Japan occupies a distinctive position. While it maintains a breeding-based supply system for Japanese macaques (Macaca fuscata) used in research, much larger numbers of wild Japanese macaques are captured and euthanized each year under legally authorized wildlife management programs. From the perspective of cumulative animal suffering, the parallel operation of these two systems appears paradoxical. This article reviews Japan's current regulations on the experimental use of wild-caught macaques, explains historically how the present situation emerged, and considers the ethical implications for internationally harmonized regulations.

title: Network analysis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder traits and mental health indicators in Brazilian adults.
abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by behavioral traits such as inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, has been widely associated with mental health impairments. However, the presence of these traits alone does not determine diagnosis, as they must also cause significant functional impairment for the individual to fulfill diagnostic criteria. Therefore, this study aimed at exploring how ADHD traits are associated with mental health indicators in general population adults regardless of whether participants met full diagnostic criteria for the disorder. The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) was used to screen ADHD traits in an online survey that also addressed mental health indicators such as excessive preoccupation, lack of meaning in life and substance use. Invitations were distributed via social media platforms. The final sample consisted of 2,159 Brazilian adult participants. Data were analyzed using network analysis. An undirected network was modeled using the Gaussian Graphical Model based on partial polychoric correlations, and regularization was applied using EBICglasso. The main network analysis was conducted for individual ADHD traits. Additional analyses were performed for the summed inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity scores, for the total ASRS summed score, and for subgroups of participants exhibiting extreme levels of trait presentation. Results indicate that, in an adult community sample, association between ADHD traits and mental health impairment is predominantly indirect. This indirect association was commonly interposed by younger age and feelings of insecurity. The results were consistent across all analyses. Overall, our results suggest that the presence of ADHD traits alone is not strongly associated with mental health impairment in the general population. We propose that both research and clinical practice may benefit from further exploring and addressing intervening factors-such as insecurity-that could underlie the association between ADHD traits and mental health impairment observed in previous studies.

title: Does the emotion regulation of self-directed humor engage the prefrontal cortex? An fNIRS study.
journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
abstract: Previous research has revealed that self-directed humor (self-enhancing and self-defeating) can help regulate negative emotions and that the prefrontal cortex (PFC) plays a critical role in emotion regulation. However, it remains unknown whether emotion regulation of self-directed humor is associated with activity in the PFC. This study mainly aims to address this issue by utilizing functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). After negative emotions were induced in participants using negative scenario texts, three regulation strategies were tested: self-enhancing humor, self-defeating humor, and cognitive reappraisal. Results showed that all three strategies significantly improved emotional valence compared with the baseline. Self-enhancing humor produced a greater increase in emotional valence than self-defeating humor, whereas neither humor condition differed significantly from cognitive reappraisal. In the fNIRS analyses, condition-specific tests against zero yielded no BH-FDR-significant channels for self-enhancing humor, one for self-defeating humor, and 25 for cognitive reappraisal. In separate repeated-measures analyses, CH4, CH5, and CH14 showed significant condition effects. Follow-up comparisons indicated higher beta values than baseline for specific active conditions, whereas the three active strategies did not differ significantly from one another in these channels. These findings support a behavioral advantage of self-enhancing over self-defeating humor in this task and identify task-related prefrontal hemodynamic correlates of the regulation conditions, without establishing that one active strategy recruits more prefrontal resources than another.

title: Investigating Tonic and Phasic Craving in Currently Drinking and Abstinent Individuals with Alcohol Use Disorder: A Preliminary Case-Control Study.
abstract: Craving is a complex construct that is not fully understood. Craving for alcohol is an important motivator of alcohol use, a known risk factor for return-to-drinking, and one of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition (DSM-5) diagnostic criteria for alcohol use disorder (AUD). Craving can be assessed retrospectively over a defined period (tonic) or in response to alcohol cues in real-time, e.g., through alcohol cue exposure (CE) paradigms (phasic). We conducted exploratory analyses of a clinical study including three matched groups: currently drinking (CD, N=9) and abstinent (AB, N=10) people with AUD and healthy controls (HC, N=12). During two alcohol CE sessions (CE1, CE2), tonic craving was assessed using the Penn Alcohol Craving Scale (PACS) and the Obsessive-Compulsive Drinking Scale (OCDS). Phasic craving was assessed using the Alcohol Urge Questionnaire (AUQ) alongside the Alcohol Attention Scale (AAS). The CD group showed higher AUQ and AAS than AB and HC groups (main effect of group, CE1: P=.048; CE2: P=.047). Group differences were also observed for tonic craving: the CD group reported higher PACS scores than HC (P=.001), while AB and CD groups showed higher OCDS scores than HC (HC vs. CD P<.0001, HC vs. AB P=.015). PACS scores correlated positively with OCDS (r=0.565, P=.001) and AUQ (r=0.595, P=.0004) scores in the full sample; within-group analyses showed a positive correlation between PACS and AUQ only in the AB group. Given the small sample size, these exploratory results should be considered preliminary and require confirmation in larger studies.

title: Effectiveness, safety and therapeutic potential of medical cannabis across treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Medical cannabis has been suggested to have a therapeutic role in selected treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. We analyzed the available evidence to assess the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. For this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, EBSCO, and PubMed for studies published between January 1, 1970, and April 25, 2026. We considered studies examining any type or formulation of medical cannabis in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Primary outcomes were disorder-specific clinical improvement measures. Safety outcomes were adverse events, serious adverse events, and withdrawals due to adverse events. Evidence from studies was synthesized as equivalent odds ratios (eORs) for comparative outcomes and as pooled proportions for single-arm safety outcomes, via random-effects meta-analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, and structured quality assessment for case series and case reports, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251148868. 127 eligible studies were included, of which 32 studies involving 3645 participants contributed to meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed improvement in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.72), refractory pain (eOR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.30-0.78), and refractory multiple sclerosis spasticity (eOR = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.07-0.75). Evidence for psychiatric disorders was scarce. Small randomized trials reported improvement in PTSD-related nightmares and cannabis dependence after failed cessation. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in hyperarousal, residual obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and refractory Tourette syndrome. Findings for treatment-resistant anxiety were inconsistent, and schizophrenia did not show a reliable therapeutic effect. Controlled analyses showed higher odds of any adverse events in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.52-3.23) and refractory multiple sclerosis (eOR = 1.89, 95% CI = 1.01-3.52), with higher odds of serious adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events also observed in drug-resistant epilepsy. In single-arm and real-world studies, pooled proportions of any adverse events ranged from 15.5% in multiple sclerosis to 66.0% in Tourette syndrome, with substantial heterogeneity. Adjunctive pharmaceutical cannabidiol has the most consistent comparative evidence for reducing seizure frequency in selected drug-resistant epilepsy. Evidence for refractory pain and multiple sclerosis is heterogeneous and varies by clinical indication, cannabinoid formulation, and outcome definition. Evidence in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders remains limited and is insufficient to support routine clinical recommendations. Further high-quality studies directly examining diagnosis-specific and formulation-specific effects, safety, and tolerability are needed. title: Comparison of Commercial Fixed and In-House Tissue-Based and Live Cell-Based Assays for the Detection of Common Neuronal Surface Autoantibodies.
abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis (AIE) is diagnosed through detection of neuronal-surface antibodies (Abs) in serum and/or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Commercial biochip-based cell-based assay (CBA) using fixed cells and in-house CBAs using live cells may give incongruent results. We aimed to shed further light on features of AIE patients with discordant CBA results to establish factors related with diagnosis and treatment-response. A total of 45 patients found positive for N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR), leucine rich glioma inactivated 1 (LGI1), contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2)-Abs on routine screening done with fixed-CBA, were further tested using in-house live-CBA and tissue-based assay (TBA). Serum neurofilament light chain (NFL) levels were measured and response to immunotherapy was assessed in a follow-up period of 36.9±7.8 months. Thirty patients who were positive on both fixed and live-CBA/TBA, showed trends towards displaying limbic symptoms and EEG/MRI features suggestive of AIE. By contrast, most of the 15 patients with only fixed-CBA positivity failed to fulfill AIE criteria. Positivity on live CBA/TBA did not predict response to immunotherapy or coexisting cancers. Some patients in the fixed-CBA positive category exhibited features highly suggestive of autoimmune encephalopathy and elevated NFL levels. Lower disease severity, presence of viral prodromal findings, absence of autonomic symptoms and facial dyskinesia were associated with treatment response. Live CBA/TBA demonstrated higher diagnostic accuracy than fixed cell-based assays and substantially reduced the likelihood of false-positive antibody detection. Positive live-CBA/TBA results strongly coincide with definite AIE criteria. However, live CBA and NFL results fail to predict response to immunotherapy and identify coexisting cancers. This is putatively because some patients in the live-CBA/TBA negative category likely have immunotherapy-responsive neuroinflammatory disorders.

title: Two Niches, One Disease: Brain and Leptomeningeal Metastases in Breast Cancer: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) metastasis is an increasingly important challenge in advanced breast cancer, yet brain parenchymal metastases (BM) and leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are often considered within a single framework despite occupying biologically distinct CNS compartments. In this narrative review, we synthesize breast cancer-specific mechanistic and clinical evidence to examine how these two forms of CNS disease differ in metastatic entry, local adaptation, molecular evolution, biomarker representation, and therapeutic vulnerability. Parenchymal BM primarily arise through haematogenous dissemination and subsequent adaptation to a neurovascular, neural, and immune-rich environment, where successful colonization requires more than blood-brain barrier traversal and is supported by reciprocal tumour-host interactions and metabolic plasticity. By contrast, LM develops within a fluid-dominated, CSF-facing compartment characterized by distinct meningeal and blood-CSF interfaces, constrained resource availability, and dynamic immune conditions. C3-C3aR-mediated barrier remodeling and LCN2-SLC22A17-dependent iron acquisition are supported mainly by experimental LM models and selected patient-derived observations, including mixed-cancer cohorts, and require broader breast cancer-specific clinical validation. Genomic and phenotypic studies further indicate that BM and LM can share metastatic ancestry while undergoing branched and compartment-associated evolution, although observed divergence may also reflect pre-existing heterogeneity, treatment selection, elapsed time, and sampling effects. Therapeutic efficacy therefore depends not only on CNS drug access but also on target expression, tumour state, niche support, disease geometry, and prior treatment. By integrating metastatic dissemination, niche adaptation, molecular evolution, biomarker representation, and therapeutic vulnerability within a single comparative framework, this review links compartment-associated biology to molecular sampling, experimental modeling, and clinical trial design. Clinically, this framework may inform compartment-specific molecular sampling and trial stratification by BM treatment status and LM presentation, although its utility for individual treatment selection requires prospective validation. Future studies combining paired multi-compartment sampling, lineage-resolved models, and serial CSF and plasma profiling will be needed to distinguish shared ancestry from niche-associated adaptation and treatment-driven evolution.

title: Social Media Use and Emotional Reactivity to Negative Stimuli: An ERP Investigation.
abstract: Exposure to violent media has long been associated with reduced emotional reactivity, empathy, and moral sensitivity, which is a phenomenon commonly referred to as emotional desensitization. Although numerous studies have explored this process in video games and films, its neural correlates in social media contexts remain insufficiently examined. This study aimed to examine whether individual differences in social media use are associated with neural responses to negative emotional stimuli. Fifty-six healthy young adults participated in an electroencephalography (EEG) experiment, during which they passively viewed negative, neutral, and positive images selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS). Emotional processing was assessed using two event-related potential (ERP) components: the Early Posterior Negativity (EPN, 200-300 ms) and the Late Positive Potential (LPP, 300-800 ms). Amplitude differences across stimulus categories and brain regions were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA. Negative images elicited significantly greater LPP amplitudes compared to neutral and positive images, particularly across central, parietal, and temporal regions, indicating sustained emotional engagement. In contrast, EPN amplitudes did not differ significantly across conditions, suggesting that early attentional mechanisms were not modulated by emotional valence. No group differences were observed between participants with high and low levels of social media use. The findings indicate that typical social media exposure was not associated with reduced neural responsiveness in this sample. Emotional engagement with negative stimuli remains intact, supporting the notion that desensitization is a gradual, context-dependent process influenced by the nature and intensity of digital exposure.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists as potential disease-modifying agents in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms, clinical trial evidence, and the neuroprotection horizon.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), originally developed as antidiabetic agents, have emerged as candidate disease-modifying therapies for Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), reflecting the widespread expression of GLP-1 receptors across neurons, glia, and the cerebral vasculature. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, clinical trial, and biomarker evidence for GLP-1 RAs in PD and AD, based on a literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched separately for trial protocols and results, through May 2026. Preclinical data implicate GLP-1 receptor agonism in anti-neuroinflammatory signaling, mitochondrial preservation, autophagy and proteostasis enhancement, anti-apoptotic effects, synaptic plasticity, cerebrovascular protection, and glymphatic clearance. Clinical evidence in PD is mixed and agent- and formulation-dependent: the phase II Exenatide-PD trial reported a motor benefit that persisted after washout (∼3.5-point between-group difference in MDS-UPDRS Part III), and the phase II LIXIPARK trial (lixisenatide) reported a significant 3.08-point between-group difference (95% CI 0.86-5.30; p = 0.007) favoring lixisenatide, whereas the larger, longer phase III Exenatide-PD3 trial, using an extended-release weekly formulation, found no significant effect on the same endpoint (adjusted coefficient 0.92; 95% CI -1.56 to 3.39; p = 0.47); oral semaglutide is under investigation in the ongoing phase II MOST-ABLE trial. In AD, the phase IIb liraglutide (ELAD) trial did not achieve statistical benefit on either its primary imaging endpoint (cerebral glucose metabolic rate; p = 0.14) or on most secondary cognitive measures, and the phase III semaglutide trials EVOKE and EVOKE+ did not meet their primary CDR-SB endpoint (estimated difference -0.08, 95% CI -0.35 to 0.20, p = 0.57 in EVOKE; 0.10, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.38, p = 0.46 in EVOKE+), despite biomarker signals including reductions in cerebrospinal fluid tau species and inflammatory markers. Comparative pharmacology reveals substantial heterogeneity in central nervous system penetration, receptor engagement, and systemic bioavailability across exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, and the imbalanced GLP-1/GIP co-agonist tirzepatide, complicating cross-agent extrapolation. Persistent challenges include separating direct neuroprotection from indirect metabolic and cardiovascular benefit, limited characterization of brain drug exposure, trial durations that may be short relative to the expected latency of a disease-modifying effect, and the absence of validated response biomarkers. We conclude that although the mechanistic and epidemiological rationale for GLP-1 RAs in neurodegeneration remains biologically plausible, current trial evidence does not yet support their use outside clinical trials, irrespective of comorbid diabetes status; future studies should prioritize earlier intervention, biomarker-guided patient selection, adequately powered subgroup analyses, and brain-penetrant formulations.

title: Adult inactivation of the Reln gene leads to disruption of cortical lamination and rhythmic activity.
abstract: Cortical cytoarchitecture and lamination are believed to remain stable after completion of development. Here, we demonstrate that early postnatal and adult (P45-P60) inactivation of the Reln gene results in dispersion of layers II and III neocortical neurons which invade layer I. In addition, neuronal mispositioning was observed in the dentate gyrus, the CA1-CA3 regions and in the cerebellum. Interestingly, inactivation of the Reln gene at adult stages resulted in altered oscillatory network activity in different cortical regions and in the nucleus accumbens. Moreover, Reelin deficiency increased depression-like behavior and impaired long-term memory consolidation. Thus, besides its crucial developmental role, Reelin is important in maintaining adult cortical lamination and rhythmic neuronal synchronization. These results suggest that, in addition to physiological and synaptic plasticity, there may be a certain degree of laminar structural plasticity in adult stages, which may lead to reconsidering the origin of layering alterations observed in neuropsychiatric diseases.

title: The dorsal vagal complex harbors a constitutively immune-enriched microglial population.
abstract: The dorsal vagal complex (DVC) comprises three anatomically and functionally linked structures, the area postrema, the nucleus tractus solitarius, and the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus nerve, forming a key hub for the integration of peripheral inflammatory information. These structures play a unique role at the neuroimmune interface, conveying peripheral immune signals to the brain and generating behavioral and physiological responses through two complementary pathways: a neural pathway, via vagal afferents projecting to the nucleus tractus solitarius, and a humoral pathway, via the area postrema, which lacks a blood-brain barrier and is therefore sensitive to circulating inflammatory mediators. Numerous studies have established that the DVC serves as a mandatory gateway for peripheral inflammatory signals, integrating this information prior to its transmission to forebrain centers and peripheral organs. Understanding this interface represents a major therapeutic challenge, as modulating the DVC and its circuits opens new avenues for the treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases and neurodegenerative disorders in which this interface is chronically disrupted. Paradoxically, despite this essential role in the regulation of inflammation, the phenotype of microglial cells, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, has received very little attention in this region. In the present study, we characterized these cells by investigating the expression of Fc receptors for IgG and major histocompatibility complex class I and II. Our results reveal microglial subpopulations displaying an atypical phenotype in the healthy DVC, suggesting that these cells may serve as a specialized immunological interface capable of actively monitoring systemic signals.

title: From cartilage degeneration to pain sensitization: a multi-tissue mitochondrial dysfunction network in osteoarthritis.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most common degenerative joint diseases, and its clinical burden arises not only from degenerative changes and synovial inflammation but is also closely associated with chronic pain, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. In patients with OA, imaging-detected structural damage and pain severity are not always consistent, suggesting that symptom persistence may also be driven by mechanisms such as metabolic disturbance, inflammatory amplification, and neural sensitization. Existing evidence indicates that mitochondrial abnormalities can be observed in cartilage, synovium, subchondral bone, and sensory nerve-related compartments, but the strength of evidence and the causal hierarchy differ across compartments. In chondrocytes, disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis is often accompanied by imbalanced energy metabolism, oxidative stress, impaired quality control, and mtDNA damage, and is associated with cell aging, regulated cell death, and matrix degeneration. Mitochondrial stress in other joint and neural compartments may participate in local inflammation, abnormal bone remodeling, and peripheral and central pain sensitization. Mitochondria-derived DAMPs, and inflammatory mediators may mediate cross-compartment interactions, but current evidence is insufficient to establish a continuous causal chain from cartilage degeneration unidirectionally to pain sensitization. Therefore, mitochondria in OA are more appropriately regarded as a pathological network shared across multiple tissue compartments and potentially interacting with one another. Building on this perspective, this article takes pain sensitization as an important dimension for understanding structural damage and symptoms in OA, and uses the "metabolism-senescence-pain axis" as a hypothesis-generating framework to review the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in OA structural degeneration, cell aging, regulated cell death, and pain sensitization, with emphasis on distinguishing evidence across cartilage, synovium, subchondral bone, sensory neurons, and central nervous system-related compartments, and to discuss potential cross-compartment interactions mediated by DAMPs, and neuroimmune signaling. Furthermore, by integrating human, animal, in vitro, and translational studies, the existing evidence is stratified, and the progress and translational barriers of mitochondria-directed and related therapeutic strategies are summarized. Finally, this article proposes future directions such as cell type-specific delivery, mitochondrial biomarkers, candidate pain mechanism phenotypes, and composite "mechanism-symptom-structure" endpoints, thereby offering a foundation for dissecting mechanistic heterogeneity, patient stratification, and precision intervention in OA.

title: Microbial metabolites as modulators of gut-brain communication in neurodegeneration: from intestinal sensing to disease initiation and progression.
abstract: How heterogeneous gut metabolite alterations relate to Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains unresolved. We propose a framework in which intestinal sensing of indole derivatives, short-chain fatty acids and bile acids links microbial function to barrier regulation and gut-brain communication. Integration denotes tissue-level convergence of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), pregnane X receptor (PXR) and metabolite-responsive G-protein-coupled receptor responses across epithelial and neighbouring immune cells, rather than an established same-cell receptor complex. Tryptophan metabolism provides an analytical focus connecting microbial indole production with host kynurenine and serotonin pathways; metabolite concentrations alone do not establish pathway flux or receptor activity. We hypothesise that suppressed indole-associated epithelial signalling, barrier hyperpermeability and peripheral immune activation could form a shared gut-derived vulnerability state in subsets of PD and AD. Its co-occurrence and temporal relationship to CNS pathology have not been prospectively demonstrated. Neural, immune and vascular processes may overlap in both diseases, with genotype and cellular context modifying relative susceptibility rather than determining exclusive pathways. Human observational findings are distinguished from experimental mechanisms and proposed interactions. Receptor-directed treatments and metabolite-based biomarkers remain candidates requiring mechanism-specific, safety and clinical validation. Whether a gut-derived intervention window exists, is reversible, or favours earlier treatment requires longitudinal and controlled studies. The framework accommodates bidirectional communication and CNS-intrinsic disease, and generates separate tests of composite gut phenotyping and genotype-metabolite interactions.

title: Neurofibromin 1 alters feeding microstructure in Drosophila.
abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is caused by the loss of neurofibromin, a protein shown to regulate metabolism and feeding behavior in Drosophila melanogaster. Using the FlyPad two-choice feeding assay, we compared feeding microstructure between NF1 null mutants, NF1 heterozygotes, and wildtype controls. We find that NF1 mutants took significantly more sips of sucrose and with greater urgency, without changes in sip duration or sucrose taste sensitivity. Overall, these results suggest loss of NF1 increases feeding frequency.

title: Posterior Circulation Stroke From Paradoxical Embolism in a Patient With Patent Foramen Ovale Dislodged During Masturbation.
