The VRC is constructed as a linear combination of coil sensitivity maps, with correlations enhanced between coil elements using the noise covariance matrix. Such a VRC ensures robust signal support across the entire brain and is used to correct phase offsets in the MORSE-derived coil sensitivity estimates, resulting in artefact-free, high-SNR phase. Compared to GRAPPA with ASPIRE phase correction, MORSE-PI demonstrates greater robustness to artefacts such as noise amplification and aliasing, and shows improved reproducibility in structural imaging at both 3 T and 7 T. Unlike ESPIRiT and GRAPPA combined with adaptive coil combination methods, MORSE-PI yields singularity-free phase maps. MORSE-PI enables high-SNR reconstructions even for the most challenging scenarios, such as single-echo EPI at 7 T. Its efficient, containerised implementation using the Gadgetron framework supports deployment on the MRI scanner console during measurements. MORSE-PI offers a flexible and computationally efficient solution for generating high-SNR, artefact- and singularity-free phase images in both single- and multi-echo GRE and EPI acquisitions. This makes it particularly well-suited for structural and functional QSM, as well as other phase-based MRI applications. Its robustness and rapid computational time facilitate efficient deployment on scanners across field strengths.

title: Defining the musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype of ochronotic arthropathy: a systematic study of 34 patients with alkaptonuria.
abstract: Ochronotic arthropathy is the leading cause of disability in patients with alkaptonuria (AKU), yet its musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSUS) phenotype has not been systematically characterized. This study aimed to define the ultrasound features of ochronotic arthropathy and identify recurring imaging patterns that may facilitate its recognition in clinical practice. We conducted a retrospective observational study including consecutive patients with genetically confirmed AKU evaluated at a tertiary referral centre between 2017 and 2025. Patients receiving nitisinone therapy and prosthetic joints were excluded from the ultrasound assessment. Bilateral standardized MSUS examinations of the shoulders, hips, knees and Achilles tendons were performed by experienced rheumatologists according to OMERACT definitions. The frequency and distribution of structural and inflammatory abnormalities were recorded, and their associations with clinical variables were explored. Thirty-four patients (17 females; mean age 52.1 ± 18.9 years) were included. Diagnostic delay positively correlated with the cumulative number of joint prostheses (ρ = 0.46, p = 0.006). The shoulder was the most frequently involved site (85.3%), showing bilateral hyperechoic rotator cuff deposits (66.7%), tendon tears (29.0%) and long head of the biceps tenosynovitis (30.0%). Knee abnormalities were identified in 61.8% of patients and included extensor tendon hyperechoic deposits (65.4%), meniscal involvement (50.0%), osteoarthritic changes (44.4%) and synovitis (29.4%). Achilles tendon involvement was observed in 48.4% of patients and was characterized by insertional and mid-portion linear hyperechoic deposits associated with tendinosis, entheseal thickening, erosive changes and only limited Power Doppler activity. Hip involvement was less common (20.0%). Significant associations were found between knee involvement and extensor mechanism abnormalities (p = 0.005) and between hip involvement and Achilles tendon enthesopathy (p = 0.038). Ochronotic arthropathy demonstrates a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound phenotype characterized by bilateral tendon and entheseal involvement, linear hyperechoic deposits, advanced tendinosis and limited inflammatory activity. These findings provide the first systematic description of the ultrasound phenotype of AKU and suggest that MSUS may represent a valuable adjunctive tool for raising clinical suspicion of ochronotic arthropathy in patients with otherwise unexplained early degenerative musculoskeletal disease. Key Points • Ochronotic arthropathy shows a distinctive musculoskeletal ultrasound pattern. • Bilateral tendon and entheseal abnormalities are highly prevalent in AKU. • Linear hyperchoic deposits frequently accompany advanced tendinosis.

title: Burnout Among Professionals in ABA-Based Services in Brazil.
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: Burnout among professionals working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)-based services has received increasing attention internationally; however, there is limited empirical data from low- and middle-income countries. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and characteristics of burnout among ABA professionals in Brazil and to examine how burnout indicators were distributed across professional and organizational characteristics within the sample. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with ABA professionals working in different regions of Brazil. Participants completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), together with a questionnaire covering demographic, professional, and work-related variables. Burnout was analyzed descriptively, with each dimension classified into low, moderate, and high categories using established cutoff scores, and distributions were examined across professional roles, age groups, academic backgrounds, salary ranges, and caseload. Burnout indicators were highly prevalent in this sample. High emotional exhaustion was identified in 77.4% of participants and low personal accomplishment (indicating greater burnout on that dimension) in 89.9%, whereas high depersonalization was less frequent (34.1%). Within this sample, the proportion of participants classified in the most severe category increased from behavior technicians to coordinators to supervisors across all three dimensions, and professionals managing more than 10 concurrent cases showed higher proportions of high depersonalization and low personal accomplishment. Categorical burnout distributions were similar across salary ranges. These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

title: The hepatic secretome-microglia axis in huntington's disease: Linking peripheral metabolic dysfunction to neuroinflammation and novel therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is traditionally regarded as a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene, resulting in selective striatal neuronal degeneration and progressive motor, cognitive, and psychiatric impairment. However, accumulating evidence indicates that HD is a systemic disorder involving profound metabolic, mitochondrial, and immune dysfunction in peripheral organs, particularly the liver. Emerging studies suggest that hepatic mitochondrial dysfunction induced by mutant huntingtin remodels the hepatic secretome through altered secretion of hepatokines, extracellular vesicles, complement proteins, inflammatory cytokines, and metabolic mediators. These circulating factors may disrupt blood-brain barrier integrity, promote microglial immunometabolic reprogramming, enhance complement-mediated synaptic pruning, and amplify chronic neuroinflammation, thereby accelerating neurodegeneration. This review summarizes current evidence supporting the liver-brain axis in HD and discusses how hepatic metabolic dysfunction contributes to central nervous system pathology. Furthermore, we highlight therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring hepatic mitochondrial homeostasis, modulating hepatokines, extracellular vesicles, exosomal microRNAs, and complement signaling to interrupt pathological liver-to-brain communication. Finally, we discuss emerging translational approaches, including multi-omics technologies, engineered extracellular vesicles, gene-editing platforms, and precision medicine, that may facilitate the development of disease-modifying therapies. By integrating peripheral metabolic regulation with central neuroimmune mechanisms, this review presents the hepatic secretome microglia axis as a potential conceptual framework for understanding HD pathogenesis and identifies liver targeted interventions as promising therapeutic opportunities beyond conventional neuron centric strategies.

title: Bioinformatic analysis of ACAD9 genetic variability.
abstract: Mitochondrial diseases (MD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders with a diagnostic rate often below 50%, mostly due to the difficulty of interpreting Variants of Unknown Significance (VUS). ACAD9 is a nuclear gene that encodes a mitochondrial protein involved in fatty acid β-oxidation and the assembly of respiratory complex I. This study aimed to refine the classification of ACAD9 missense VUS through an integrative computational approach combining in silico, evolutionary and structural analysis. A gene-specific dataset of missense pathogenic, benign and uncertain significance variants was curated from public databases (HGMD, ClinVar, GnomAD, UniProt or LOVD) and in-house sequencing data. Thirty-five in silico pathogenicity predictors were retrieved from the dbNSFP v5.3 and benchmarked using the datasets. Predictor performance was evaluated using 10 metrics and the top predictors were integrated with evolutionary conservation (ConSurf), structural modelling (PyMOL, HOPE) and thermodynamic stability analysis (FoldX) to re-evaluate 17 VUS. Predictor performance for ACAD9 variants varied significantly. Because no statistically significant differences were detected among the ten highest-ranked predictors, ClinPred, MetaRNN, PHACTboost, MutationTaster and REVEL were selected as the top stability-informed predictors. The integrative predictive and structural analysis reclassified 8 variants as "likely pathogenic" and 5 as "likely benign", while 4 remained classified as VUS due to conflicting evidence. A gene-specific, multi-layered computational strategy substantially improves VUS classification in ACAD9. These in silico findings provide strong, albeit non-definitive, evidence to guide diagnostic efforts. It should be complemented with functional validation, which remains essential to confirm pathogenicity.

title: Exclusive oscillator interactions generate globally coherent phase arrangements: insights from benchmark traveling salesman problems.
abstract: Various oscillatory phenomena are observed in nature. Oscillatory interactions can contribute to the self-organization of globally coherent relationships and may play important roles in information processing, control, and communication in biological systems. However, the mechanisms by which such relationships are generated remain unclear. This study used the traveling salesman problem, a classic combinatorial optimization problem, as a benchmark to investigate whether exclusive interactions between Kuramoto phase oscillators can generate globally coherent phase arrangements through self-organization. We assigned cities to individual oscillators and introduced mutual repulsive interactions based on inter-city distances and phase differences. Our analyses showed that the oscillators frequently converged to phase orders corresponding to the shortest tour, although two-cluster solutions were also observed for some distance sets. Even when two-cluster solutions emerged, adding a new oscillator at a sufficiently large distance from the existing oscillators markedly increased the probability of obtaining the shortest-tour solution. In a special case, convergence to the shortest tour was also successfully demonstrated in simulations with up to 50 oscillators. These findings suggest that exclusive oscillator interactions can generate globally coherent phase arrangements through self-organization and provide a simple framework for investigating biologically inspired collective dynamics. Although a precise mathematical understanding of these dynamics remains a subject for future investigation, the present framework provides a platform for exploring oscillator-based computation through self-organized phase dynamics.

title: TotalSpineSeg: automated whole-spine vertebral segmentation with high robustness to labeling errors.
abstract: To develop TotalSpineSeg, a robust tool for vertebrae and intervertebral disc instance segmentation, along with spinal cord and spinal canal segmentation, capable of processing any 3D medical image regardless of contrast, resolution, or field of view, while overcoming fusion and fragmentation errors common in standard segmentation. A two-stage cascaded deep learning model was trained on 1404 MRIs. To explicitly prevent errors where adjacent vertebrae merge or a single vertebra splits, the architecture employs a novel "odd/even" representation. The second stage is conditioned on an odd-intervertebral disc mask from the first stage to assign distinct semantic classes to alternating vertebrae, enforcing accurate separation between neighboring vertebrae. Finally, a landmark-based logic uses key anatomical points (C2-C3, C7-T1, T12-L1, and L5-S) to anchor sequential labeling, while a localizer-based strategy ensures accurate identification even in truncated, short field-of-view scans. Evaluation across diverse contrasts and pathologies yielded a vertebral identification rate of 96.22% on localizer MRI and generalized to CT scans with a 92.87% identification rate. For intervertebral disc instance labeling, where vertebral separation is not mandatory, both model stages attained 99% labeling accuracy with a mean positional L2 error of 1.55 mm, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. TotalSpineSeg successfully generalizes to diverse 3D medical images, overcoming variations in contrast, resolution, and field of view. The proposed topological constraints effectively eliminate vertebral fusion and fragmentation errors, delivering a state-of-the-art identification rate for both vertebrae and intervertebral discs across MRI and CT modalities. Question Can a topology-constrained framework overcome heterogeneous contrasts and resolution limits, including localizers, to ensure robust, automated vertebral and disc labeling? Findings TotalSpineSeg achieved a high identification rate across diverse contrasts, localizers, and CT, surpassing state-of-the-art methods by eliminating fusion and fragmentation errors. Clinical relevance TotalSpineSeg enables fully automated biomarker extraction from clinical scans, allowing precise assessment of stenosis, lesions, and atrophy against normative ranges.

title: Beyond the brain: curcumin as a multi-target neuropharmacological modulator of the gut-brain axis in major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Curcumin, the principal polyphenol of Curcuma longa, has been proposed as a multi-target neuropharmacological agent for neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. We propose that major depressive disorder (MDD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) share a convergent gut-brain axis dysfunction, and that curcumin can serve as a pharmacological probe to test whether this convergent pathway is causally relevant. This narrative review evaluates that hypothesis. We conducted a structured literature search across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and CNKI using predefined search terms. This is a narrative review with a structured search strategy rather than a systematic review; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis was performed. From 2256 identified records, 112 primary studies were selected for synthesis after dual screening and consensus resolution. Findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than as a quantitative synthesis. We propose a differential metabolite-sensitivity threshold model as a testable hypothesis: shared dysbiosis-related metabolic and inflammatory disturbances may affect serotonergic function earlier than dopaminergic function because depressed mood manifests at modest neurotransmitter deficits, whereas nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons possess substantial compensatory reserve. Preclinical studies indicate that curcumin exerts prebiotic-like effects, promotes short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, suppresses NF-κB-dependent neuroinflammation, restores BDNF signaling, inhibits α-synuclein aggregation, and improves depressive- and PD-like behaviors. These actions map onto convergent gut-brain pathways involving short-chain fatty acid deficiency, tryptophan-kynurenine imbalance, monoaminergic precursor depletion, and neuroinflammation. This model generates four testable predictions: (P1: functional dysbiosis convergence; P2: temporal precedence of depressed mood; P3: curcumin's multi-node modulation; and P4: clinical benefit with adequate bioavailability). Preclinical evidence supports functional convergence (P1), temporal asymmetry (P2), and curcumin's multi-target actions (P3), but clinical benefit in MDD-PD comorbidity (P4) remains untested. However, curcumin's clinical translation remains limited by poor oral bioavailability (~ 1% for standard extracts) and the absence of randomized trials in MDD-PD comorbidity. We conclude that the convergent gut-brain hypothesis is plausible, partially supported, and directly testable, and we specify the minimal studies required to confirm or falsify it.

title: Antibiotic Exposure and Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Systemic antibiotics may disrupt the gut and oral microbiome, potentially affecting anticancer treatment efficacy. Their prognostic relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), particularly during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations between systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation and oncologic outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 2015 to March 28, 2026. Eligible studies included patients with HNSCC or NPC receiving ICI, definitive CRT, or chemo-immunotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), or objective response rate (ORR). Random-effects models pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for OS and PFS; ORR was synthesized descriptively. Risk of bias was assessed, as appropriate, using ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, RoB 2, or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Eleven studies involving 6,293 patients were included; nine studies (4,507 patients) contributed to survival meta-analyses. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse OS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.08) and PFS (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.28-1.96). Associations were consistent in ICI-treated cohorts (OS HR 1.80, 95% CI 1.53-2.13; PFS HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.24-2.25) and CRT cohorts (OS HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.32; PFS HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.11-2.11). Heterogeneity was low-to-moderate for OS (I2=28.6%) and negligible for PFS (I2=0%). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable OS (HR range 1.76-1.86) and PFS estimates (1.58-1.63). Worse OS was observed for both 30-60-day pre-ICI exposure (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.43-2.90) and concurrent/peri-treatment exposure (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.49-2.04). ORR was descriptively lower in antibiotic-exposed patients. Most studies had serious/high risk of bias, primarily due to confounding by indication. Systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation is associated with inferior survival and response in HNSCC and NPC. However, predominantly observational evidence and substantial confounding preclude causal inference. Prospective microbiome-informed studies are needed.
keywords: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Head and Neck

title: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 in a North Indian endogamous community: clinical and genetic insights from multigenerational families.
abstract: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2 (SCA2) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the ATXN2 gene. Endogamous populations may exhibit clustering of inherited disorders because of founder effects and restricted gene flow. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic features of SCA2 in multigenerational Banjara families from North India. A total of 141 individuals from 23 multigenerational Banjara families were clinically evaluated. 55 clinically affected individuals and at-risk family members underwent molecular testing for ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions using flanking PCR followed by capillary electrophoresis. Clinical characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics, and the relationship between CAG repeat length and age at onset was assessed by linear regression. Pathogenic ATXN2 CAG repeat expansions were identified in 39 of the 55 individuals who underwent genetic testing (70.9%), including 32 symptomatic individuals and seven asymptomatic carriers. The expanded alleles ranged from 33 to 48 CAG repeats (mean 41.6 ± 3.3). Gait ataxia was the most common presenting symptom. A significant inverse correlation was observed between CAG repeat length and age at onset (R² = 0.71, P < 0.0001). In this study, we found SCA2 across multiple multigenerational Banjara families from North India. The inverse relationship between ATXN2 CAG repeat length and age at onset was also observed in our cohort. The presence of asymptomatic carriers highlights the importance of early molecular diagnosis, family-based genetic counselling, and targeted screening in high-risk families.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in patients with minor stroke is associated with lower risk of post-stroke dementia.
abstract: Minor ischemic stroke is associated with increased risks of post-stroke dementia independent of stroke recurrence, yet there are no guideline-recommended therapies targeted at cognitive outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to be associated with lower risk of dementia among diabetes patients; however, their effect on cognitive outcomes among minor stroke patients is largely unknown. This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2016-2025). Adult patients with minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5 and non-disabling) were included. Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, cognitive impairment, or dementia were excluded. GLP-1RA use was defined as a prescription prior to or within 3 months of stroke diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 75 baseline characteristics, outcomes were assessed over a 5 year follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. After propensity score matching, 1,425 patients per group were analyzed. Mean age was 60.7 years, with diabetes present in 92.7% and mean HbA1c of 8.7%. GLP-1RA use was associated with a 48% lower hazard of post-stroke dementia (3.4% vs. 7.0%, HR 0.52 [95% CI 0.37-0.74]) and a 31% lower hazard of other neurocognitive complaints (17.2% vs 25.6%, HR 0.69 [95% CI 0.59-0.81]) over 5 years. GLP-1RA use was also associated with reduced mortality (4.4% vs. 8.8%; HR 0.57 [95% CI 0.42-0.77]) and major ischemic stroke (1.5% vs. 2.7%; HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.35-1.01]). No significant difference in intracranial hemorrhage rates was observed. Among this cohort of minor ischemic stroke patients mostly with concomitant diabetes, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced risks of post-stroke dementia and other neurocognitive complaints. These findings support prioritizing GLP-1RA use for diabetic patients who suffered minor ischemic stroke. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm causality and determine optimal implementation.

title: DNA Flexibility Depends on the Length of the CAG Repeat Tract in the ATXN2 Gene.
abstract: The ATXN2 gene is located on chromosome 12q24.1 and encodes the ataxin-2 protein, which is involved in the regulation of RNA metabolism, protein synthesis, and intracellular signaling. The CAG tract encoding glutamine can cause expansion, leading to a range of neurodegenerative diseases. Our theoretical results show that expansion of the CAG tract in the ATXN2 gene induces intrinsic mechanical instability at the DNA level. Even under weak, physiologically relevant torsional stress, the expanded CAG region forms collective conformational states and pronounced bending, acting as a structural hot spot. This phenomenon can be considered a novel mechanistic contributor to the development of ataxia type 2 (SCA2). It is important to note that these effects arise without the formation of open states in DNA, suggesting that instability emerges at an earlier stage than those described by known mechanisms. Thus, this mechanism does not replace established RNA- or protein-mediated models of toxicity but rather complements them by accounting for the mechanical contribution to DNA dynamics, which may predispose the ATXN2 locus to genomic instability and pathological progression.

title: Concepts in Practice: Understanding and Addressing Name-Based Microaggressions in Health Care.
abstract: Names are important markers of identity, culture, and belonging. In health care settings, individuals with ethnically distinct names may experience repeated mispronunciations, unsolicited nicknames, or avoidance of their names. Repeated mispronunciations without sincere efforts to learn or improve, as well as the avoidance, dismissal, or replacement of names with unsolicited nicknames, may function as name-based microaggressions and can negatively affect psychological safety, professional identity formation, and workplace inclusion. In this manuscript, we discuss the effect of name-based microaggressions on health care professionals and trainees, with particular focus on the emergency department. We review the 3 major categories of microaggressions-microassaults, microinsults, and microinvalidations-and use clinical vignettes to demonstrate how these behaviors may appear in both interpersonal and institutional settings. We also propose practical interpersonal and institutional strategies to promote more inclusive workplaces and foster respectful engagement with ethnically distinct names. By encouraging greater awareness, curiosity, humility, and intentionality around names, health care organizations can help cultivate clinical environments where individuals feel respected, included, and valued.

title: Bibliometric Analysis and Cluster Analysis of Research Trends on Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Patients After Anesthesia.
journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
abstract: The purpose of this study was to analyze research on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and to identify research hotspots and trends. A bibliometric analysis. We searched the Web of Science Core Collection for English-language publications on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia published from 1988 to 2024. The retrieved data were analyzed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R 4.3.3. A total of 1,119 articles were included in the analysis. Among countries, China had the highest number of publications. Among institutions, Harvard University ranked first, with 165 publications. Among journals, Anesthesiology had the highest total number of citations, with 3,074 citations and an impact factor of 9.1. Among authors, Xie Zhongcong had the largest number of publications, with 24 articles and 1,045 citations. Keyword cluster analysis identified seven major research themes: anesthesia approach, risk, and clinical management; pathophysiological mechanisms and neuroinflammation; cardiovascular surgery and perioperative monitoring; biomarkers and neurodegeneration; anesthetic drugs and assessment tools; outcomes and neurophysiological responses; and recommendations. High-frequency keywords such as "anesthesia," "surgery," and "dysfunction" reflected the main research hotspots and trends in this field. This bibliometric study summarizes the research landscape of postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and identifies major contributors, research hotspots, and evolving trends. The findings may provide a useful reference for future research in this field.
